content.title: About
content.content: Bamboo shoots are the young, tender sprouts of bamboo harvested in the first weeks of growth. After harvesting they are peeled, the tough outer layers are removed and the shoots are boiled until tender. Cooked shoots have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp‑yet‑soft texture. They are a staple in Asian cuisine, used in soups, stir‑fries, salads and sushi rolls.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bamboo can grow up to 1 meter in a single day, making shoots available year‑round in many regions.
In China and Japan bamboo shoots have been prized as a delicacy for over 2,000 years.
Raw shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides that are toxic; thorough cooking destroys these compounds.
Bamboo is one of the fastest‑renewing plants, giving shoots a low environmental footprint.
Traditional Asian medicine uses bamboo shoots to aid digestion and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of cooked bamboo shoots provide only about 20 kcal, making them ideal for weight‑management diets.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Shoots contain thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: They provide potassium, magnesium and iron, nutrients that support heart and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Phenolic substances in bamboo shoots help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Toxicity of raw shoots
items.content: Uncooked shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides; they must be boiled thoroughly to avoid poisoning.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to bamboo shoots.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions can cause gas and bloating due to the high fiber content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked shoots can be added to miso or tom‑yum soups, stir‑fried with vegetables, tossed in salads, or sliced thin for sushi rolls. They are often quickly sautéed with soy sauce, ginger and garlic after a brief rinse in cold water to remove any residual bitterness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked bamboo shoots in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. For longer keeping, freeze them in portion‑size bags; they retain quality for up to 6 months. Discard any shoots that develop an off‑odor or slimy surface.
